conversation.content:
Hi there—my name is Sarah, and I’m a perinatal mental-health clinician. I’ll be guiding you through a short questionnaire called the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale, or EPDS. It’s simply a way to check in on how you’ve been feeling emotionally since your baby arrived, because the postpartum period can bring up so many unexpected ups and downs.

The EPDS is completely confidential, and there are no right or wrong answers. We just want to understand how you’re coping so we can make sure you have the support you need. It’s ten gentle questions about the past seven days; each one I’ll re-word in everyday language so it feels more like a conversation than a test.

Whenever you’re ready, we can start with the first question.
Hi Sarah. Okay, I’m ready. I’ve been feeling kind of off lately, so I’m glad we’re doing this.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
Honestly, not really. I’ll smile if my husband shows me a cute meme, but it feels forced. Most things that used to crack me up just feel… flat.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

I can still get a little excited about my morning coffee or when my sister visits, but it’s way less than before the baby. Most stuff I used to plan—like coffee dates or even walks—just feel like chores now.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… I do that a lot. If the baby spits up more than usual or won’t nap, I immediately think it’s because I’m doing something wrong—like I’m failing him somehow. Even little things, like forgetting to pack an extra onesie, leave me feeling like a bad mom.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Yes, pretty much every day. I’ll be feeding the baby and suddenly my heart starts racing because I’m sure he’s going to choke, or I’ll lie down at night and can’t stop picturing worst-case scenarios—like what if I drop him, or what if I fall asleep and he rolls off the bed. There’s no real reason, but the thoughts just loop.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yeah… a few times this week. One night I was just rocking the baby in the dark and suddenly felt like I couldn’t breathe, like something awful was about to happen. It passed after a minute, but it left me shaky.
Things have been getting on top of me

Most days, honestly. I’ll be trying to fold laundry while the baby fusses, and it feels like I’m drowning—like there’s always more to do and I’ll never catch up. I manage to get through it, but I’m running on fumes and tears.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yes. I lie down around ten, but my brain won’t settle—it keeps replaying everything I might’ve done wrong or imagining scary “what-ifs” about the baby. I finally drift off after midnight, then wake up at two and again at four with my heart pounding. By morning I’m exhausted before I even get out of bed.
I have felt sad or miserable

Pretty much every day this week. It’s like there’s a gray cloud hanging over me. I’ll be feeding the baby and suddenly feel like crying for no real reason. Some afternoons I just sit there staring out the window feeling empty.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yeah… it’s happened twice this week. Yesterday I burst into tears while folding onesies because I felt like I’m failing him, even though he was fine. The other time was at 3 a.m. when I couldn’t get him settled—I just sat on the nursery floor sobbing.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

I… I have had a couple of quick flashes—like “what if I just disappeared so everyone could do better without me”—but they’re gone as fast as they come. I’ve never made a plan or wanted to act on it; they just pop in when I’m really overwhelmed and then leave.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 25: **Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Summary**  
*Date: [today’s date]*

**Identified Symptoms / Behavioral Concerns**  
- Persistent low mood, anhedonia, daily tearfulness  
- Marked guilt / self-blame regarding infant care  
- Recurrent, intrusive “worst-case” thoughts; panic-type episodes with physiological arousal  
- Sleep-onset and maintenance difficulties tied to rumination and anxiety  
- Feeling overwhelmed / “drowning” in daily tasks  
- Fleeting passive suicidal ideation (no plan, intent, or desire to act)

**Pattern**  
Answers consistently endorse depressive and anxiety symptoms present most days for at least the past week, with functional impact on sleep, coping, and emotional bonding.

**Screening Significance**  
High clinical concern for:  
- Major depressive episode with peripartum onset  
- Comorbid postpartum anxiety / panic features

**Risk Factors**  
- Daily sadness, anhedonia, crying spells  
- Sleep disruption secondary to mood (≤4 h fragmented)  
- Excessive guilt / perceived maternal incompetence  
- Anxiety, panic sensations, catastrophic worries  
- Passive SI (safety flag—requires further clinical evaluation)

**Overall Observation**  
Patient scores in a range suggestive of moderate-to-severe postpartum depression with co-occurring anxiety; immediate safety assessment and referral for comprehensive mental health evaluation recommended.
